verses.text: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was blameless and upright, one who feared God, and turned away from evil.
There were born to him seven sons and three daughters.
He had seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she-donkeys, and very many servants; so that this man was the greatest of all the people of the east.
His sons used to go and hold a feast in the house of each on his day; and they would send and invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

And when the days of the feast had run their course, Job would send and sanctify them, and he would rise early in the morning and offer burnt offerings according to the number of them all; for Job said, “It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts.” Thus Job did continually.
Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came among them.
The LORD said to Satan, “From where have you come?” Satan answered the LORD, “From going back and forth on the earth, and from walking up and down on it.”
And the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, who fears God and turns away from evil?”
Then Satan answered the LORD, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
Have you not put a hedge about him and his house and all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land.
But put forth your hand now, and touch all that he has, and he will curse you to your face.”
And the LORD said to Satan, “Behold, all that he has is in your power; only upon himself do not put forth your hand.” So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD.
Now there was a day when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house;
and there came a messenger to Job, and said, “The oxen were plowing and the donkeys feeding beside them;
and the Sabe'ans fell upon them and took them, and slew the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
While he was yet speaking, there came another, and said, “The fire of God fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them; and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

While he was yet speaking, there came another, and said, “The Chalde'ans formed three companies, and made a raid upon the camels and took them, and slew the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
While he was yet speaking, there came another, and said, “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house;
and behold, a great wind came across the wilderness, and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young people, and they are dead; and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell upon the ground, and worshiped.
And he said, “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return; the LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.”
In all this Job did not sin or charge God with wrong.
Again there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came among them to present himself before the LORD.
And the LORD said to Satan, “From where have you come?” Satan answered the LORD, “From going back and forth on the earth, and from walking up and down on it.”

And the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, who fears God and turns away from evil? He still holds fast his integrity, although you moved me against him, to destroy him without cause.”
Then Satan answered the LORD, “Skin for skin! All that a man has he will give for his life.
But put forth your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse you to your face.”
And the LORD said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your power; only spare his life.”
So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD, and afflicted Job with loathsome sores from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.
And he took a potsherd with which to scrape himself, and sat among the ashes.
Then his wife said to him, “Do you still hold fast your integrity? Curse God, and die.”
But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” In all this Job did not sin with his lips.

Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come upon him, they came each from his own place, Eli'phaz the Te'manite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zo'phar the Na'amathite. They made an appointment together to come to condole with him and comfort him.
And when they saw him from afar, they did not recognize him; and they raised their voices and wept; and they tore their robes and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.
And they sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his suffering was very great.
After this Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
And Job said:
“Let the day perish wherein I was born,
Let that day be darkness!
Let gloom and deep darkness claim it.
That night—let thick darkness seize it!
Yes, let that night be barren;
Let those curse it who curse the day,
Let the stars of its dawn be dark;
because it did not shut the doors of my mother’s womb,
“Why did I not die at birth,
Why did the knees receive me?
For then I should have lain down and been quiet;
with kings and counselors of the earth
or with princes who had gold,
Or why was I not as a hidden untimely birth,
There the wicked cease from troubling,
There the prisoners are at ease together;
The small and the great are there,
“Why is light given to him who is in misery,
who long for death, but it comes not,
who rejoice exceedingly,
Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden,
For my sighing comes as my bread,
For the thing that I fear comes upon me,
I am not at ease, nor am I quiet;
Then Eli'phaz the Te'manite answered:
“If one ventures a word with you, will you be offended?
Behold, you have instructed many,
Your words have upheld him who was stumbling,
But now it has come to you, and you are impatient;
Is not your fear of God your confidence,
“Think now, who that was innocent ever perished?
As I have seen, those who plow iniquity
By the breath of God they perish,
The roar of the lion, the voice of the fierce lion,
The strong lion perishes for lack of prey,
“Now a word was brought to me stealthily,
Amid thoughts from visions of the night,
dread came upon me, and trembling,
A spirit glided past my face;
It stood still,
‘Can mortal man be righteous before God?
Even in his servants he puts no trust,
how much more those who dwell in houses of clay,
Between morning and evening they are destroyed;
If their tent-cord is plucked up within them,
“Call now; is there any one who will answer you?
Surely vexation kills the fool,
I have seen the fool taking root,
His sons are far from safety,
His harvest the hungry eat,
For affliction does not come from the dust,
but man is born to trouble
“As for me, I would seek God,
who does great things and unsearchable,
he gives rain upon the earth
he sets on high those who are lowly,
He frustrates the devices of the crafty,
He takes the wise in their own craftiness;
They meet with darkness in the daytime,
But he saves the fatherless from their mouth,
So the poor have hope,
“Behold, happy is the man whom God reproves;
For he wounds, but he binds up;
He will deliver you from six troubles;
In famine he will redeem you from death,
You shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue,
At destruction and famine you shall laugh,
For you shall be in league with the stones of the field,
You shall know that your tent is safe,
You shall know also that your descendants shall be many,
You shall come to your grave in ripe old age,
Behold, this we have searched out; it is true.
Then Job answered:
“O that my vexation were weighed,
For then it would be heavier than the sand of the sea;
For the arrows of the Almighty are in me;
Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass,
Can that which is tasteless be eaten without salt,
My appetite refuses to touch them;
“O that I might have my request,
that it would please God to crush me,
This would be my consolation;
What is my strength, that I should wait?
Is my strength the strength of stones,
In truth I have no help in me,
“He who withholds kindness from a friend
My brethren are treacherous as a torrent-bed,
which are dark with ice,
In time of heat they disappear;
The caravans turn aside from their course;
The caravans of Te'ma look,
They are disappointed because they were confident;
Such you have now become to me;
Have I said, ‘Make me a gift’?
Or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand’?
“Teach me, and I will be silent;
How forceful are honest words!
Do you think that you can reprove words,
You would even cast lots over the fatherless,
“But now, be pleased to look at me;
Turn, I beg, let no wrong be done.
Is there any wrong on my tongue?
“Has not man a hard service upon earth,
Like a slave who longs for the shadow,
so I am allotted months of emptiness,
When I lie down I say, ‘When shall I arise?’
My flesh is clothed with worms and dirt;
My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle,
“Remember that my life is a breath;
The eye of him who sees me will behold me no more;
As the cloud fades and vanishes,
he returns no more to his house,
“Therefore I will not restrain my mouth;
Am I the sea, or a sea monster,
When I say, ‘My bed will comfort me,
then you scare me with dreams
so that I would choose strangling
I loathe my life; I would not live for ever.
What is man, that you make so much of him,
visit him every morning,
How long will you not look away from me,
If I sin, what do I do to you, you watcher of men?
Why do you not pardon my transgression
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:
“How long will you say these things,
Does God pervert justice?
If your children have sinned against him,
If you will seek God
if you are pure and upright,
And though your beginning was small,
“For inquire, I beg you, of bygone ages,
for we are but of yesterday, and know nothing,
Will they not teach you, and tell you,
“Can papyrus grow where there is no marsh?
While yet in flower and not cut down,
Such are the paths of all who forget God;
His confidence breaks in sunder,
He leans against his house, but it does not stand;
He thrives before the sun,
His roots twine about the stone-heap;
If he is destroyed from his place,
Behold, this is the joy of his way;
“Behold, God will not reject a blameless man,
He will yet fill your mouth with laughter,
Those who hate you will be clothed with shame,
Then Job answered:
“Truly I know that it is so:
If one wished to contend with him,
He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength
he who removes mountains, and they know it not,
who shakes the earth out of its place,
who commands the sun, and it does not rise;
who alone stretched out the heavens,
who made the Bear and Ori'on,
who does great things beyond understanding,
Behold, he passes by me, and I see him not;
Behold, he snatches away; who can hinder him?
“God will not turn back his anger;
How then can I answer him,
Though I am innocent, I cannot answer him;
If I summoned him and he answered me,
For he crushes me with a tempest,
he will not let me get my breath,
If it is a contest of strength, behold him!
Though I am innocent, my own mouth would condemn me;
I am blameless; I regard not myself;
It is all one; therefore I say,
When disaster brings sudden death,
The earth is given into the hand of the wicked;
“My days are swifter than a runner;
They go by like skiffs of reed,
If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint,
I become afraid of all my suffering,
I shall be condemned;
If I wash myself with snow,
yet you will plunge me into a pit,
For he is not a man, as I am, that I might answer him,
There is no umpire between us,
Let him take his rod away from me,
Then I would speak without fear of him,
“I loathe my life;
I will say to God, Do not condemn me;
Does it seem good to you to oppress,
Do you have eyes of flesh?
Are your days as the days of man,
that you seek out my iniquity
although you know that I am not guilty,
Your hands fashioned and made me;
Remember that you have made me of clay;
Did you not pour me out like milk
You clothed me with skin and flesh,
You have granted me life and mercy;
Yet these things you hid in your heart;
If I sin, you mark me,
If I am wicked, woe to me!
And if I lift myself up, you hunt me like a lion,
you renew your witnesses against me,
“Why did you bring me forth from the womb?
and were as though I had not been,
Are not the days of my life few?
before I go from where I shall not return,
the land of gloom and chaos,
Then Zo'phar the Na'amathite answered:
“Should a multitude of words go unanswered,
Should your babble silence men,
For you say, ‘My doctrine is pure,
But oh, that God would speak,
and that he would tell you the secrets of wisdom!
“Can you find out the deep things of God?
It is higher than heaven —what can you do?
Its measure is longer than the earth,
If he passes through, and imprisons,
For he knows worthless men;
But a stupid man will get understanding,
“If you set your heart aright,
If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away,
Surely then you will lift up your face without blemish;
You will forget your misery;
And your life will be brighter than the noonday;
And you will have confidence, because there is hope;
You will lie down, and none will make you afraid;
But the eyes of the wicked will fail;
Then Job answered:
“No doubt you are the people,
But I have understanding as well as you;
I am a laughingstock to my friends;
In the thought of one who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune;
The tents of robbers are at peace,
“But ask the beasts, and they will teach you;
or the plants of the earth, and they will teach you;
Who among all these does not know
In his hand is the life of every living thing
Does not the ear try words
Wisdom is with the aged,
“With God are wisdom and might;
If he tears down, none can rebuild;
If he withholds the waters, they dry up;
With him are strength and wisdom;
He leads counselors away stripped,
He looses the bonds of kings,
He leads priests away stripped,
He deprives of speech those who are trusted,
He pours contempt on princes,
He uncovers the deeps out of darkness,
He makes nations great, and he destroys them:
He takes away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth,
They grope in the dark without light;
“Behold, my eye has seen all this,
What you know, I also know;
But I would speak to the Almighty,
As for you, you whitewash with lies;
Oh, that you would keep silent,
Hear now my reasoning,
Will you speak falsely for God,
Will you show partiality toward him,
Will it be well with you when he searches you out?
He will surely rebuke you
Will not his majesty terrify you,
Your maxims are proverbs of ashes,
“Let me have silence, and I will speak,
I will take my flesh in my teeth,
Behold, he will slay me; I have no hope;
This will be my salvation,
Listen carefully to my words,
Behold, I have prepared my case;
Who is there that will contend with me?
Only grant two things to me,
withdraw your hand far from me,
Then call, and I will answer;
How many are my iniquities and my sins?
Why do you hide your face,
Will you frighten a driven leaf
For you write bitter things against me,
You put my feet in the stocks,
Man wastes away like a rotten thing,
“Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.
He comes forth like a flower, and withers;
And do you open your eyes upon such a one
Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean?
Since his days are determined,
look away from him, and desist,
“For there is hope for a tree,
Though its root grow old in the earth,
yet at the scent of water it will bud
But man dies, and is laid low;
As waters fail from a lake,
so man lies down and rises not again;
Oh, that you would hide me in Sheol,
If a man die, shall he live again?
You would call, and I would answer you;
For then you would number my steps,
my transgression would be sealed up in a bag,
“But the mountain falls and crumbles away,
the waters wear away the stones;
You prevail for ever against him, and he passes;
His sons come to honor, and he does not know it;
He feels only the pain of his own body,
Then Eli'phaz the Te'manite answered:
“Should a wise man answer with windy knowledge,
Should he argue in unprofitable talk,
But you are doing away with the fear of God,
For your iniquity teaches your mouth,
Your own mouth condemns you, and not I;
“Are you the first man that was born?
Have you listened in the council of God?
What do you know that we do not know?
Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us,
Are the consolations of God too small for you,
Why does your heart carry you away,
that you turn your spirit against God,
What is man, that he can be clean?
Behold, God puts no trust in his holy ones,
how much less one who is abominable and corrupt,
“I will show you, hear me;
(what wise men have told,
to whom alone the land was given,
The wicked man writhes in pain all his days,
Terrifying sounds are in his ears;
He does not believe that he will return out of darkness,
He wanders abroad for bread, saying, ‘Where is it?’
distress and anguish terrify him;
Because he has stretched forth his hand against God,
running stubbornly against him
because he has covered his face with his fat,
and has lived in desolate cities,
he will not be rich, and his wealth will not endure,
he will not escape from darkness;
Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself;
It will be paid in full before his time,
He will shake off his unripe grape, like the vine,
For the company of the godless is barren,
They conceive mischief and bring forth evil
Then Job answered:
“I have heard many such things;
Shall windy words have an end?
I also could speak as you do,
I could strengthen you with my mouth,
“If I speak, my pain is not assuaged,
Surely now God has worn me out;
And he has shriveled me up,
He has torn me in his wrath, and hated me;
Men have gaped at me with their mouth,
God gives me up to the ungodly,
I was at ease, and he broke me asunder;
his archers surround me.
He breaks me with breach upon breach;
I have sewn sackcloth upon my skin,
My face is red with weeping,
although there is no violence in my hands,
“O earth, cover not my blood,
Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven,
My friends scorn me;
that he would maintain the right of a man with God,
For when a few years have come
My spirit is broken, my days are extinct,
Surely there are mockers about me,
“Lay down a pledge for me with yourself;
Since you have closed their minds to understanding,
He who informs against his friends to get a share of their property,
“He has made me a byword of the peoples,
My eye has grown dim from grief,
Upright men are appalled at this,
Yet the righteous holds to his way,
But you, come on again, all of you,
My days are past, my plans are broken off,
They make night into day;
If I look for Sheol as my house,
if I say to the pit, ‘You are my father,’
where then is my hope?
Will it go down to the bars of Sheol?
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:
“How long will you hunt for words?
Why are we counted as cattle?
You who tear yourself in your anger,
“Yes, the light of the wicked is put out,
The light is dark in his tent,
His strong steps are shortened
For he is cast into a net by his own feet,
A trap seizes him by the heel,
A rope is hid for him in the ground,
Terrors frighten him on every side,
His strength is hunger-bitten,
By disease his skin is consumed,
He is torn from the tent in which he trusted,
In his tent dwells that which is none of his;
His roots dry up beneath,
His memory perishes from the earth,
He is thrust from light into darkness,
He has no offspring or descendant among his people,
They of the west are appalled at his day,
Surely such are the dwellings of the ungodly,
Then Job answered:
“How long will you torment me,
These ten times you have cast reproach upon me;
And even if it be true that I have erred,
If indeed you magnify yourselves against me,
know then that God has put me in the wrong,
Behold, I cry out, ‘Violence!’ but I am not answered;
He has walled up my way, so that I cannot pass,
He has stripped from me my glory,
He breaks me down on every side, and I am gone,
He has kindled his wrath against me,
His troops come on together;
“He has put my brethren far from me,
My kinsfolk and my close friends have failed me;
the guests in my house have forgotten me;
I call to my servant, but he gives me no answer;
I am repulsive to my wife,
Even young children despise me;
All my intimate friends abhor me,
My bones cling to my skin and to my flesh,
Have pity on me, have pity on me, O you my friends,
Why do you, like God, pursue me?
“Oh, that my words were written!
Oh, that with an iron pen and lead
For I know that my Redeemer lives,
If you say, ‘How we will pursue him!’
be afraid of the sword,
Then Zo'phar the Na'amathite answered:
“Therefore my thoughts answer me,
I hear censure which insults me,
Do you not know this from of old,
that the exulting of the wicked is short,
Though his height mount up to the heavens,
he will perish for ever like his own dung;
He will fly away like a dream, and not be found;
The eye which saw him will see him no more,
His children will seek the favor of the poor,
His bones are full of youthful vigor,
“Though wickedness is sweet in his mouth,
though he is loath to let it go,
yet his food is turned in his stomach;
He swallows down riches and vomits them up again;
He will suck the poison of asps;
He will not look upon the rivers,
He will give back the fruit of his toil,
For he has crushed and abandoned the poor,
“Because his greed knew no rest,
There was nothing left after he had eaten;
In the fulness of his sufficiency he will be in straits;
To fill his belly to the full
He will flee from an iron weapon;
It is drawn forth and comes out of his body,
Utter darkness is laid up for his treasures;
The heavens will reveal his iniquity,
The possessions of his house will be carried away,
This is the wicked man’s portion from God,
Then Job answered:
“Listen carefully to my words,
Bear with me, and I will speak,
As for me, is my complaint against man?
Look at me, and be appalled,
When I think of it I am dismayed,
Why do the wicked live,
Their children are established in their presence,
Their houses are safe from fear,
Their bull breeds without fail;
They send forth their little ones like a flock,
They sing to the tambourine and the lyre,
They spend their days in prosperity,
They say to God, ‘Depart from us!
What is the Almighty, that we should serve him?
Behold, is not their prosperity in their hand?
“ How often is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out?
That they are like straw before the wind,
You say, ‘God stores up their iniquity for their sons.’
Let their own eyes see their destruction,
For what do they care for their houses after them,
Will any teach God knowledge,
One dies in full prosperity,
his body full of fat
Another dies in bitterness of soul,
They lie down alike in the dust,
“Behold, I know your thoughts,
For you say, ‘Where is the house of the prince?
Have you not asked those who travel the roads,
that the wicked man is spared in the day of calamity,
Who declares his way to his face,
When he is borne to the grave,
The clods of the valley are sweet to him;
How then will you comfort me with empty nothings?
Then Eli'phaz the Te'manite answered:
“Can a man be profitable to God?
Is it any pleasure to the Almighty if you are righteous,
Is it for your fear of him that he reproves you,
Is not your wickedness great?
For you have exacted pledges of your brothers for nothing,
You have given no water to the weary to drink,
The man with power possessed the land,
You have sent widows away empty,
Therefore snares are round about you,
your light is darkened, so that you cannot see,
“Is not God high in the heavens?
Therefore you say, ‘What does God know?
Thick clouds enwrap him, so that he does not see,
Will you keep to the old way
They were snatched away before their time;
They said to God, ‘Depart from us,’
Yet he filled their houses with good things—
The righteous see it and are glad;
saying, ‘Surely our adversaries are cut off,
“Agree with God, and be at peace;
Receive instruction from his mouth,
If you return to the Almighty and humble yourself,
if you lay gold in the dust,
and if the Almighty is your gold,
then you will delight yourself in the Almighty,
You will make your prayer to him, and he will hear you;
You will decide on a matter, and it will be established for you,
For God abases the proud,
He delivers the innocent man;
Then Job answered:
“Today also my complaint is bitter,
Oh, that I knew where I might find him,
I would lay my case before him
I would learn what he would answer me,
Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power?
There an upright man could reason with him,
“Behold, I go forward, but he is not there;
on the left hand I seek him, but I cannot behold him;
But he knows the way that I take;
My foot has held fast to his steps;
I have not departed from the commandment of his lips;
But he is unchangeable and who can turn him?
For he will complete what he appoints for me;
Therefore I am terrified at his presence;
God has made my heart faint;
for I am hemmed in by darkness,
“Why are not times of judgment kept by the Almighty,
Men remove landmarks;
They drive away the donkey of the fatherless;
They thrust the poor off the road;
Behold, like wild donkeys in the desert
They gather their fodder in the field
They lie all night naked, without clothing,
They are wet with the rain of the mountains,
(There are those who snatch the fatherless child from the breast,
They go about naked, without clothing;
among the olive rows of the wicked they make oil;
From out of the city the dying groan,
“There are those who rebel against the light,
The murderer rises in the dark,
The eye of the adulterer also waits for the twilight,
In the dark they dig through houses;
For deep darkness is morning to all of them;
“You say, ‘They are swiftly carried away upon the face of the waters;
Drought and heat snatch away the snow waters;
The squares of the town forget them;
“They feed on the barren childless woman,
Yet God prolongs the life of the mighty by his power;
He gives them security, and they are supported;
They are exalted a little while, and then are gone;
If it is not so, who will prove me a liar,
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:
“Dominion and fear are with God;
Is there any number to his armies?
How then can man be righteous before God?
Behold, even the moon is not bright
how much less man, who is a maggot,
Then Job answered:
“How you have helped him who has no power!
How you have counseled him who has no wisdom,
With whose help have you uttered words,
The shades below tremble,
Sheol is naked before God,
He stretches out the north over the void,
He binds up the waters in his thick clouds,
He covers the face of the moon,
He has described a circle upon the face of the waters
The pillars of heaven tremble,
By his power he stilled the sea;
By his wind the heavens were made fair;
Behold, these are but the outskirts of his ways;
And Job again took up his discourse, and said:
“As God lives, who has taken away my right,
as long as my breath is in me,
my lips will not speak falsehood,
Far be it from me to say that you are right;
I hold fast my righteousness, and will not let it go;
“Let my enemy be as the wicked,
For what is the hope of the godless when God cuts him off,
Will God hear his cry,
Will he take delight in the Almighty?
I will teach you concerning the hand of God;
Behold, all of you have seen it yourselves;
“This is the portion of a wicked man with God,
If his children are multiplied, it is for the sword;
Those who survive him the pestilence buries,
Though he heap up silver like dust,
he may pile it up, but the just will wear it,
The house which he builds is like a spider’s web,
He goes to bed rich, but will do so no more;
Terrors overtake him like a flood;
The east wind lifts him up and he is gone;
It hurls at him without pity;
It claps its hands at him,
“Surely there is a mine for silver,
Iron is taken out of the earth,
Men put an end to darkness,
They open shafts in a valley away from where men live;
As for the earth, out of it comes bread;
Its stones are the place of sapphires,
“That path no bird of prey knows,
The proud beasts have not trodden it;
“Man puts his hand to the flinty rock,
He cuts out channels in the rocks,
He binds up the streams so that they do not trickle,
“But where shall wisdom be found?
Man does not know the way to it,
The deep says, ‘It is not in me,’
It cannot be gotten for gold,
It cannot be valued in the gold of O'phir,
Gold and glass cannot equal it,
No mention shall be made of coral or of crystal;
The topaz of Ethiopia cannot compare with it,
“From where does wisdom come?
It is hidden from the eyes of all living,
Abad'don and Death say,
“God understands the way to it,
For he looks to the ends of the earth,
When he gave to the wind its weight,
when he made a decree for the rain,
then he saw it and declared it;
And he said to man,
And Job again took up his discourse, and said:
“Oh, that I were as in the months of old,
when his lamp shone upon my head,
as I was in my autumn days,
when the Almighty was yet with me,
when my steps were washed with milk,
When I went out to the gate of the city,
the young men saw me and withdrew,
the princes refrained from talking,
the voice of the nobles was hushed,
When the ear heard, it called me blessed,
because I delivered the poor who cried,
The blessing of him who was about to perish came upon me,
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me;
I was eyes to the blind,
I was a father to the poor,
I broke the fangs of the unrighteous,
Then I thought, ‘I shall die in my nest,
my roots spread out to the waters,
my glory fresh with me,
“Men listened to me, and waited,
After I spoke they did not speak again,
They waited for me as for the rain;
I smiled on them when they had no confidence;
I chose their way, and sat as chief,
“But now they make sport of me,
What could I gain from the strength of their hands,
Through want and hard hunger
they pick mallow and the leaves of bushes,
They are driven out from among men;
In the gullies of the torrents they must dwell,
Among the bushes they bray;
A senseless, a disreputable brood,
“And now I have become their song,
They abhor me, they keep aloof from me;
Because God has loosed my cord and humbled me,
On my right hand the rabble rise,
They break up my path,
As through a wide breach they come;
Terrors are turned upon me;
“And now my soul is poured out within me;
The night racks my bones,
With violence it seizes my garment;
God has cast me into the mire,
I cry to you and you do not answer me;
You have turned cruel to me;
You lift me up on the wind, you make me ride on it,
Yes, I know that you will bring me to death,
“Yet does not one in a heap of ruins stretch out his hand,
Did not I weep for him whose day was hard?
But when I looked for good, evil came;
My heart is in turmoil, and is never still;
I go about blackened, but not by the sun;
I am a brother of jackals,
My skin turns black and falls from me,
My lyre is turned to mourning,
“I have made a covenant with my eyes;
What would be my portion from God above,
Does not calamity befall the unrighteous,
Does not he see my ways,
“If I have walked with falsehood,
(Let me be weighed in a just balance,
if my step has turned aside from the way,
then let me sow, and another eat;
“If my heart has been enticed to a woman,
then let my wife grind for another,
For that would be a heinous crime;
for that would be a fire which consumes unto Abad'don,
“If I have rejected the cause of my manservant or my maidservant,
what then shall I do when God rises up?
Did not he who made me in the womb make him?
“If I have withheld anything that the poor desired,
or have eaten my morsel alone,
(for from his youth I reared him as a father,
if I have seen any one perish for lack of clothing,
if his loins have not blessed me,
if I have raised my hand against the fatherless,
then let my shoulder blade fall from my shoulder,
For I was in terror of calamity from God,
“If I have made gold my trust,
if I have rejoiced because my wealth was great,
if I have looked at the sun when it shone,
and my heart has been secretly enticed,
this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges,
“If I have rejoiced at the ruin of him that hated me,
(I have not let my mouth sin
if the men of my tent have not said,
(the sojourner has not lodged in the street;
if I have concealed my transgressions from men,
because I stood in great fear of the multitude,
Oh, that I had one to hear me!
Surely I would carry it on my shoulder;
I would give him an account of all my steps;
“If my land has cried out against me,
if I have eaten its yield without payment,
let thorns grow instead of wheat,
So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
Then Eli'hu the son of Bar'achel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, became angry. He was angry at Job because he justified himself rather than God;
he was angry also at Job’s three friends because they had found no answer, although they had declared Job to be in the wrong.
Now Eli'hu had waited to speak to Job because they were older than he.
And when Eli'hu saw that there was no answer in the mouths of these three men, he became angry.
And Eli'hu the son of Bar'achel the Buzite answered:
I said, ‘Let days speak,
But it is the spirit in a man,
It is not the old that are wise,
Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me;
“Behold, I waited for your words.
I gave you my attention,
Beware lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom;
He has not directed his words against me,
“They are discomfited, they answer no more;
And shall I wait, because they do not speak,
I also will give my answer;
For I am full of words,
Behold, my heart is like wine that has no vent;
I must speak, that I may find relief;
I will not show partiality to any person
For I do not know how to flatter,
“But now, hear my speech, O Job,
Behold, I open my mouth;
My words declare the uprightness of my heart,
The spirit of God has made me,
Answer me, if you can;
Behold, I am toward God as you are;
Behold, no fear of me need terrify you;
“Surely, you have spoken in my hearing,
You say, ‘I am clean, without transgression;
Behold, he finds occasions against me,
he puts my feet in the stocks,
“Behold, in this you are not right. I will answer you.
Why do you contend against him,
For God speaks in one way,
In a dream, in a vision of the night,
then he opens the ears of men,
that he may turn man aside from his deed,
he keeps back his soul from the Pit,
“Man is also chastened with pain upon his bed,
so that his life loathes bread,
His flesh is so wasted away that it cannot be seen;
His soul draws near the Pit,
If there be for him an angel,
and he is gracious to him, and says,
let his flesh become fresh with youth;
then man prays to God, and he accepts him,
and he sings before men, and says:
He has redeemed my soul from going down into the Pit,
“Behold, God does all these things,
to bring back his soul from the Pit,
Give heed, O Job, listen to me;
If you have anything to say, answer me;
If not, listen to me;
Then Eli'hu said:
“Hear my words, you wise men,
for the ear tests words
Let us choose what is right;
For Job has said, ‘I am innocent,
in spite of my right I am counted a liar;
What man is like Job,
who goes in company with evildoers
For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing
“Therefore, hear me, you men of understanding,
For according to the work of a man he will repay him,
Of a truth, God will not do wickedly,
Who gave him charge over the earth
If he should take back his spirit to himself,
all flesh would perish together,
“If you have understanding, hear this;
Shall one who hates justice govern?
who says to a king, ‘Worthless one,’
who shows no partiality to princes,
In a moment they die;
“For his eyes are upon the ways of a man,
There is no gloom or deep darkness
For he has not appointed a time for any man
He shatters the mighty without investigation,
Thus, knowing their works,
He strikes them for their wickedness
because they turned aside from following him,
so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him,
When he is quiet, who can condemn?
that a godless man should not reign,
“For has any one said to God,
teach me what I do not see;
Will he then make repayment to suit you,
Men of understanding will say to me,
‘Job speaks without knowledge,
Would that Job were judged to the end,
For he adds rebellion to his sin;
And Eli'hu said:
“Do you think this to be just?
that you ask, ‘What advantage have I?
I will answer you
Look at the heavens, and see;
If you have sinned, what do you accomplish against him?
If you are righteous, what do you give to him;
Your wickedness concerns a man like yourself,
“Because of the multitude of oppressions people cry out;
But none says, ‘Where is God my Maker,
who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth,
There they cry out, but he does not answer,
Surely God does not hear an empty cry,
How much less when you say that you do not see him,
And now, because his anger does not punish,
Job opens his mouth in empty talk,
And Eli'hu continued, and said:
“Bear with me a little, and I will show you,
I will fetch my knowledge from afar,
For truly my words are not false;
“Behold, God is mighty, and does not despise any;
He does not keep the wicked alive,
He does not withdraw his eyes from the righteous,
And if they are bound in fetters
then he declares to them their work
He opens their ears to instruction,
If they listen and serve him,
But if they do not listen, they perish by the sword,
“The godless in heart cherish anger;
They die in youth,
He delivers the afflicted by their affliction,
He also allured you out of distress
“But you are full of the judgment on the wicked;
Beware lest wrath entice you into scoffing;
Will your cry avail to keep you from distress,
Do not long for the night,
Take heed, do not turn to iniquity,
Behold, God is exalted in his power;
Who has prescribed for him his way,
“Remember to extol his work,
All men have looked on it;
Behold, God is great, and we know him not;
For he draws up the drops of water,
which the skies pour down,
Can any one understand the spreading of the clouds,
Behold, he scatters his lightning about him,
For by these he judges peoples;
He covers his hands with the lightning,
Its crashing declares concerning him,
“At this also my heart trembles,
Listen to the thunder of his voice
Under the whole heaven he lets it go,
After it his voice roars;
God thunders wondrously with his voice;
For to the snow he says, ‘Fall on the earth’;
He seals up the hand of every man,
Then the beasts go into their lairs,
From its chamber comes the whirlwind,
By the breath of God ice is given,
He loads the thick cloud with moisture;
They turn round and round by his guidance,
Whether for correction, or for his land,
“Hear this, O Job;
Do you know how God lays his command upon them,
Do you know the balancings of the clouds,
you whose garments are hot
Can you, like him, spread out the skies,
Teach us what we shall say to him;
Shall it be told him that I would speak?
“And now men cannot look on the light
Out of the north comes golden splendor;
The Almighty—we cannot find him;
Therefore men fear him;
Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind:
“Who is this that darkens counsel by words without knowledge?
Gird up your loins like a man,
“Where were you when I laid the foundation of the earth?
Who determined its measurements—surely you know!
On what were its bases sunk,
when the morning stars sang together,
“Or who shut in the sea with doors,
when I made clouds its garment,
and prescribed bounds for it,
and said, ‘Thus far shall you come, and no farther,
“Have you commanded the morning since your days began,
that it might take hold of the skirts of the earth,
It is changed like clay under the seal,
From the wicked their light is withheld,
“Have you entered into the springs of the sea,
Have the gates of death been revealed to you,
Have you comprehended the expanse of the earth?
“Where is the way to the dwelling of light,
that you may take it to its territory
You know, for you were born then,
“Have you entered the storehouses of the snow,
which I have reserved for the time of trouble,
What is the way to the place where the light is distributed,
“Who has cleft a channel for the torrents of rain,
to bring rain on a land where no man is,
to satisfy the waste and desolate land,
“Has the rain a father,
From whose womb did the ice come forth,
The waters become hard like stone,
“Can you bind the chains of the Plei'ades,
Can you lead forth the Maz'zaroth in their season,
Do you know the ordinances of the heavens?
“Can you lift up your voice to the clouds,
Can you send forth bolts of lightning, that they may go
Who has put wisdom in the clouds,
Who can number the clouds by wisdom?
when the dust runs into a mass
“Can you hunt the prey for the lion,
when they crouch in their dens,
Who provides for the raven its prey,
“Do you know when the mountain goats bring forth?
Can you number the months that they fulfil,
when they crouch, bring forth their offspring,
Their young ones become strong, they grow up in the open;
“Who has let the wild donkey go free?
to whom I have given the steppe for his home,
He scorns the tumult of the city;
He ranges the mountains as his pasture,
“Is the wild ox willing to serve you?
Can you bind him in the furrow with ropes,
Will you depend on him because his strength is great,
Do you have faith in him that he will return,
“The wings of the ostrich wave proudly;
For she leaves her eggs to the earth,
forgetting that a foot may crush them,
She deals cruelly with her young, as if they were not hers;
because God has made her forget wisdom,
When she rouses herself to flee,
“Do you give the horse his might?
Do you make him leap like the locust?
He paws in the valley, and exults in his strength;
He laughs at fear, and is not dismayed;
Upon him rattle the quiver,
With fierceness and rage he swallows the ground;
When the trumpet sounds, he says ‘Aha!’
“Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars,
Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up
On the rock he dwells and makes his home
From there he spies out the prey;
His young ones suck up blood;
And the LORD said to Job:
“Shall a faultfinder contend with the Almighty?
Then Job answered the LORD:
“Behold, I am of small account; what shall I answer you?
I have spoken once, and I will not answer;
Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind:
“Gird up your loins like a man;
Will you even put me in the wrong?
Have you an arm like God,
“Deck yourself with majesty and dignity;
Pour forth the overflowings of your anger,
Look on every one that is proud, and bring him low;
Hide them all in the dust together;
Then will I also acknowledge to you,
“Behold, Be'hemoth,
Behold, his strength in his loins,
He makes his tail stiff like a cedar;
His bones are tubes of bronze,
“He is the first of the works of God;
For the mountains yield food for him
Under the lotus plants he lies,
For his shade the lotus trees cover him;
Behold, if the river is turbulent he is not frightened;
Can one take him with hooks,
“Can you draw out Levi'athan with a fishhook,
Can you put a rope in his nose,
Will he make many supplications to you?
Will he make a covenant with you
Will you play with him as with a bird,
Will traders bargain over him?
Can you fill his skin with harpoons,
Lay hands on him;
Behold, the hope of a man is disappointed;
No one is so fierce that he dares to stir him up.
Who has given to me, that I should repay him?
“I will not keep silence concerning his limbs,
Who can strip off his outer garment?
Who can open the doors of his face?
His back is made of rows of shields,
One is so near to another
They are joined one to another;
His sneezings flash forth light,
Out of his mouth go flaming torches;
Out of his nostrils comes forth smoke,
His breath kindles coals,
In his neck abides strength,
The folds of his flesh cling together,
His heart is hard as a stone,
When he raises himself up the mighty are afraid;
Though the sword reaches him, it does not avail;
He counts iron as straw,
The arrow cannot make him flee;
Clubs are counted as stubble;
His underparts are like sharp potsherds;
He makes the deep boil like a pot;
Behind him he leaves a shining wake;
Upon earth there is not his like,
He beholds everything that is high;
Then Job answered the LORD:
“I know that you can do all things,
‘Who is this that hides counsel without knowledge?’
‘Hear, and I will speak;
I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear,
therefore I despise myself,

Now therefore take seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept his prayer not to deal with you according to your folly; for you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has.”
So Eli'phaz the Te'manite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zo'phar the Na'amathite went and did what the LORD had told them; and the LORD accepted Job’s prayer.
And the LORD restored the fortunes of Job, when he had prayed for his friends; and the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.

Then came to him all his brothers and sisters and all who had known him before, and ate bread with him in his house; and they showed him sympathy and comforted him for all the evil that the LORD had brought upon him; and each of them gave him a piece of money and a ring of gold.
And the LORD blessed the latter days of Job more than his beginning; and he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she-donkeys.
He had also seven sons and three daughters.
And he called the name of the first Jemi'mah; and the name of the second Kezi'ah; and the name of the third Ker'en-hap'puch.
And in all the land there were no women so fair as Job’s daughters; and their father gave them inheritance among their brothers.
And after this Job lived a hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, four generations.
And Job died, an old man, and full of days.
